generator.why: Batches of 8 to 48 with means within ±5 and standard deviations from 1 to 10, the scale of normalized activations; gamma, beta and dy within ±3. The numpy generator draws means to ±5000 with deviations down to 0.001, which float32 cannot represent apart, and batches of 2, whose dx is pure cancellation (about 5e-5) that float32's rounding noise exceeds. Stored cases keep the full range.

skip.large-mean-tiny-spread: A batch mean of 2000 with a standard deviation of 0.008: float32 rounds the mean itself by more than the answer can absorb, so even the two-pass formula is off by ~1e-3. No float32-scale stand-in separates the formulas reliably (the window is a mean-to-spread ratio of roughly 40 to 100); the one-pass E[x²] − E[x]² shortcut still fails the stored gen-1-3.
skip.gen-1-2: A baked draw from the numpy generator's full range: column means in the thousands with spreads down to 0.001, which float32 cannot hold apart, so two correct float32 solutions disagree. The twin's own generator draws float32-scale batches instead.
